transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called us together to begin the capital-review process for the payment-processing resilience facility. As you know, the vendor has provided a preliminary capital estimate of $10 million with commissioning targeted for Q4 2026. Before I can authorize this capital, our normal review routine requires me to check with each of you — FP&A, tax, procurement, and information security. I'd like to go around the table and hear any concerns, constraints, or information each of you has that I should factor into the authorization decision. Let's start with FP&A — what do we need to document on the approved capital envelope?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a security review finding. My review identified an internal-audit requirement, confirmed in a memo this morning, that an independent penetration test and remediation sign-off must occur before the facility connects to production. This control has not yet been added to the project checklist, and it needs to be incorporated before we finalize authorization, as it could affect both the schedule and potentially the scope of work with the vendor.

transcript.text: I finalized the updated capital forecast this morning. The board-approved capital envelope for this facility is exactly $8,400,000 — not the $10 million preliminary vendor estimate. The project remains value-accretive only at or below that $8.4 million threshold. I should note the board expects this project to be authorized at the $8.4 million envelope with appropriate conditions rather than declined, once the review items are addressed. This revised forecast has not yet been circulated to you, Elena, so I'm putting it on the record now. For the capital-review documentation, FP&A will record the approved envelope as $8,400,000.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a commercial issue on the procurement side. I obtained the vendor's signed commercial position this week, which allows the bank to retain exactly 15% of each equipment invoice until performance acceptance. However, the draft purchase order still shows payment in full on delivery. We need to correct the PO terms to reflect the agreed retention before authorization is finalized — this protects the bank's position and aligns our payment terms with the performance acceptance milestone.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a tax-credit issue. I confirmed in a tax memo received yesterday that the equipment for this facility qualifies for an exactly $1,200,000 investment tax credit — but only if it is commissioned on or before December 31, 2026, and the tax-credit election is included in the approval package. I have not yet attached the memo to the capital request. Given the vendor's Q4 2026 commissioning target, this credit is at risk if there are any schedule slippages, and the election needs to be formally made in the authorization package to capture it.
